newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs shuffle sideways in dull market.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs shuffle sideways in dull market.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures shuffled aimlessly in thin trade on Wednesday as a lack of new leads and year-end apathy kept players in the wings.
"It's an end-of-year market and nobody's really reacting to anything," said a Japanese bank dealer, adding that comments by the Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor had only a fleeting impact.
BOJ governor Yasuo Matsushita said Japan's economic recovery was starting to gain firmness and monetary policy would emphasise securing the basis for recovery.
He also said the central bank would continue its outright purchases of JGBs if necessary, but dealers said the comments were merely a reiteration of what he has said in the past.

"The Nikkei looks like it's heading into a bearish trend, which could have some impact on Euroyen and JGBs," said the dealer. The 225-share Nikkei average shed 320.43 points to close at its day low of 20,093.03.
The lead September Euroyen contract stood at 99.24 at 1110 GMT against an IMM close at 99.26. March JGBs settled at 125.49 against their previous 125.66.
Eurodollar futures finished steady with the most active March contract unchanged against its IMM close at 94.43.
"It's very difficult for March to move above 94.50 but it's also difficult for it to close below 94.40 so we'll just be stuck in a range for a while," said the dealer.
